title: Noise operator bound for bounded-degree functions
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fourier degree at most $k$, meaning every nonzero Fourier coefficient is indexed by a set of size at most $k$. For every real $\rho\ge1$, the $L^2$ norm under the uniform measure satisfies $\|T_\rho f\|_2\le\rho^k\|f\|_2$, where $T_\rho$ multiplies the Fourier coefficient at each set $S$ by $\rho^{|S|}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ have Fourier degree at most $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $\rho\ge1$. For the Fourier multiplier $\widehat{T_\rho f}(S)=\rho^{|S|}\widehat f(S)$, one has $\|T_\rho f\|_2\le\rho^k\|f\|_2$ under the uniform measure. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
